newsitem.title: USA: US high-yld bonds get a reprieve, high-grades firm.
newsitem.headline: US high-yld bonds get a reprieve, high-grades firm.

text.p: Gains in the U.S. Treasury and stock markets gave a temporary reprieve to the ailing high-yield bond arena and prices finished up 1/4 to 1/2 point on a broad basis, dealers said.
Investment grade spreads were firmer in quiet trade as dealers there remained focused on big new issues, including a minimum of $2.0 billion in debt from J.C. Penney Co Inc as early as Tuesday.
Topping high-yield trade, bonds of Mesa Inc rose nearly six points after news the company signed a definitive agreement to merge with Parker & Parsley Petroleum Co.
Mesa Operating Co's 10-5/8 percent cash pay bonds were quoted at 109-1/4 near the close compared with Friday's 103-1/2 bid. One trader quoted them at 110 bid.

The two companies will create Pioneer Natural Resources Co, a U.S. independent oil and gas exploration company. Under the terms of the agreement, Mesa stockholders will receive one share of Pioneer stock for every seven Mesa shares. Parker & Parsley stockholders will receive one Pioneer share for every one of theirs.

T. Michael Hoye, a high-yield analyst with KDP Investment Advisors Inc, said on a proforma basis the cash flow to interest coverage ratio would improve from 1.7 times for Mesa in 1996 to 3.4 times for Pioneer. Total debt to invested capital would fall significantly, he added.
Pioneer's enterprise value would be about $4.2 billion including $1.3 billion in combined debt outstanding.

Elsewhere, traders said a 20 tick rally for the Treasury bond and 30 point gains in the Dow Industrials served as reasons for investors to test the waters, albeit quietly. Larger gains were spotty with some telecoms outperforming.

TCI Satellite Inc's 10-7/8 percent debt, one of the hardest hit issues in the recent correction, were seen higher at 90-1/2 bid. Telewest Communications zero coupon bonds, downgraded by Standard & Poor's last week, rose to 66-1/2 from 65-3/4 on Friday.
Sterling Chemical Inc's 11-1/4 percent 10-year notes, priced at a discount last Wednesday, rose to a 101-5/8 bid.

Turning to high-grades, activity was thin all day with Alex Brown Inc and BankAmerica Corp paper benefitting from a merger and review for upgrade, respectively. New issues of last week firmed after facing some indigestion, traders said.
Specifically, Alex Brown debt due 2005 tightened between five and 10 basis points in light trade on news it will merge with Bankers Trust New York Corp in a stock swap valued at about $1.7 billion.
Bankers Trust debt was little changed, traders said. Its stock fell 2-3/8 to 79-7/8.

BankAmerica Corp debt tightened about two basis points after Moody's Investors Service said it may raise the firms ratings. The news came as little surprise to the Street and failed to spur much trading, dealers said.

New issues showed signs of stability. GTE's $500 million 7.51 percent debt, which priced at 67 basis points over the curve, was unchanged at 70 bid, 68 offered. Philip Morris' $500 million 7-1/2 percent debt, which priced at 75 basis points over, tightened marginally to 76 bid, 73 offer compared with wide trades of 78 to 79 late last week, traders said.

But alas, action was considered quiet ahead of new issues. J.C. Penney's deal, managed by Credit Suisse First Boston, may garner spreads as tight as 45 basis points in five years, 70 basis points in 10 years, 85 basis points in 20 years, 120 basis points in 30 years, and 40 basis points for a 40-year bond with a 10-year put option.
